title: Climate Resilience Assessment of Rural Farming Households: A Review of Tools and Frameworks
content: This study aims to evaluate tools and frameworks used to measure climate resilience of rural farming households and illuminate gaps and potential future directions to guide subsequent research and policy initiatives. A review of literature was conducted using electronic database Web of Science from peer reviewed articles written in English spanning the period from 2013 to 2023. The key search terms were, “tools and frameworks to assess climate resilience of rural farmers.” Results show that conceptual frameworks do not measure resilience, they give structure and guide indicator selection while participatory tools give farmers experiences and context specific assessments. Index based approaches provide measurable and comparable results allowing statistical rigor and appropriate policy formulation. Most tools and frameworks that measure resilience, however, lack standardized indicators as they may require large data sets or there are some overlapping indicators across frameworks or there is limited integration of qualitative and quantitative data. In conclusion, no single tool is sufficient to measure climate resilience of rural farmers. It is recommended that the most effective tools should combine conceptual frameworks, structure and sound theory, with quantitative indices for measurement and evaluation and incorporate participatory tools for farmer experience and relevance as climate resilience is context specific.
